stories.title: The AI trade cracked: Nvidia lost about $450 billion in a day, and the same day foreigners poured ₹14,975 crore into India
stories.label: HOT
stories.window: Fri 6 to Sat 7 Nov. Post tonight; it goes stale once Monday's markets move.
happening: Thu 5 Nov, New York: a sell-off led by AI and chip stocks. The Nasdaq fell 5.5%, its steepest slide since April 2025; the S&P 500 fell 4.4%, its worst day since the April 2025 'Liberation Day' tariffs; the Dow fell more than 1,800 points (CNBC; AP via Yahoo Finance).

Nvidia fell more than 9% and lost almost $450 billion in market value (CNBC). Qualcomm also fell more than 9% on a weak forecast; AMD, Micron and Applied Materials fell by double digits; Tesla and SpaceX more than 9% (CNBC). AP's version gives Nvidia -8% and AMD -14%; the figures moved through the day.

Why, per the reports: fears that the AI data-centre buildout will slow after the Democrats swept Congress (possible moratoriums, rules on power and water, voters wary of higher power bills), expensive borrowing, and critics who say AI stocks were in a bubble (AP; CNBC). South Korea's Kospi fell 5.3% (AP).

Same day, Mumbai (the Indian session closed before New York opened): the Sensex rose 2,008.61 points (2.60%) to 79,310.01 and the Nifty 576 points to 24,536.60. Over six sessions the Sensex gained 6,063.98 points (8.27%), and investors' notional wealth rose ₹28.92 lakh crore (Business Today; Times of India).

Foreign investors bought a net ₹14,975 crore of Indian shares on 5 Nov, the largest single-day inflow in more than a year (Whalesbook). On Wed 4 Nov they bought about $770 million, their biggest day since October 2025, and they have been net buyers of ₹39,404 crore over 13 sessions since 16 Oct, after a record $29 billion outflow earlier (Times of India). The Times of India links the hope of more foreign money to a global shift away from AI trades; Business Today notes that AI-heavy Taiwan and Korea crashed while India rose.
curiosity_gaps: All year the reason given for India's falling market was that foreign money had gone to AI stocks in the US, Taiwan and Korea. On the day the AI trade cracked, foreigners bought India harder than on any day in more than a year.

Nvidia lost almost $450 billion of market value in one session (CNBC), while Indian investors' wealth rose ₹28.92 lakh crore over the six days to the same Thursday (Business Today). Two markets, one day, opposite stories.
Which is it for your portfolio this Diwali: the Indian rally, or the US crash in your Nasdaq fund or US-stocks app?

facts.text: 5 Nov: Nasdaq -5.5%, steepest since April 2025; Nvidia down more than 9%, almost $450 bn of market value lost; Qualcomm down more than 9%; AMD, Micron, Applied Materials down double digits; reasons: AI buildout seen slowing after the Democratic sweep, rising rates, capital needs.

5 Nov: Sensex +2,008.61 (2.60%) to 79,310.01; Nifty +576 to 24,536.60; six-session Sensex gain 6,063.98 points; investor wealth +₹28.92 lakh crore in six sessions; AI-heavy Taiwan and Korea indices crashed.

Six sessions: Sensex +8.27%; FIIs bought about $769.65 mn on Wed 4 Nov, the biggest since October 2025; net buyers of ₹39,404 crore over 13 sessions since 16 Oct; earlier record outflow $29 bn; a global shift away from AI trades raised hopes of more inflows; Nifty -6.1% and Sensex -6.9% for 2026 so far.

Nvidia's fall differs by source (CNBC more than 9%, AP 8%); use '$450 billion', which only CNBC gives, with credit, or 'about 9%'.

The causal link (AI money leaving, India gaining) is the reports' reading, not a fact; say 'analysts say'. India's Friday open may reverse the rally after the US crash: re-check before the voice is recorded.

stories.title: Stockal: US broker DriveWealth says the unauthorised access came through Stockal's app; nearly 30 investors, ₹100 crore+ alleged
stories.label: HOT
stories.window: About 12 Nov: the cybersecurity review, regulators and police will keep turning it.
happening: Recap: on 15 Oct someone logged into 26 Stockal accounts with valid credentials; in 13, large-cap US holdings were sold and the money put into thinly traded microcaps; no funds were withdrawn (Borderless, Stockal's parent).

New since yesterday's desk: DriveWealth, the US broker and custodian, disputes responsibility. It says the unauthorised activity came through Stockal's customer interface, that it froze the affected accounts on Stockal's instructions, and that it is working with Borderless to examine the trades (FinanceFeeds, citing Moneycontrol, 5 Nov). Moneycontrol's headline: 'DriveWealth denies role in unauthorised trades' (5 Nov).

A police complaint registered in Bengaluru names Stockal, the Borderless companies, DriveWealth and HDFC Securities (HDFC Securities says its partnership ended in July 2024). Being named establishes nothing yet.

Two investor cases: one had about $335,768 of 10 US holdings sold, and the proceeds bought 300,000 Zhibao Technology shares at about $1.05; he estimates a loss of about $450,000 (₹4.26 crore). Another says a portfolio of about $3.1 million (₹29 crore) was sold within two minutes and 3.05 million shares of a thinly traded company bought within 15. Zhibao fell nearly 60%, closing at $0.42 on 23 Oct (FinanceFeeds).
curiosity_gaps: Nobody withdrew a rupee, yet the money is mostly gone: it was turned into a Chinese microcap that then fell 60%.
Now the Indian app and the American broker each say the hole was on the other side. When it's your account, who answers?

facts.text: Nearly 30 investors; ₹100 crore+ (preliminary, from investor accounts); 26 accounts accessed, 13 with large-cap sales and microcap buys; no funds withdrawn; one investor's $335,768 → 300,000 Zhibao at about $1.05, estimated loss about $450,000 (₹4.26 crore); another about $3.1 mn (₹29 crore) sold in two minutes; Zhibao down nearly 60% to $0.42 on 23 Oct; DriveWealth says access came through Stockal's interface and accounts were frozen on Stockal's instructions; Bengaluru complaint names Stockal, Borderless, DriveWealth, HDFC Securities; HDFC Securities' partnership ended July 2024.
Borderless: valid credentials used; no breach of its own systems found; possible social engineering (unconfirmed); help 'in good faith', not an admission.
One investor: 10 holdings incl. 150 Apple, 234.8 Tesla, 400 Nvidia sold on 15 Oct; emailed on 18 Oct.

watch_out: Allegations under investigation: 'investors allege', 'DriveWealth says', 'Borderless says'. Don't call it a scam by Stockal, and don't say who did it.
Counts: 13 accounts traded (company), nearly 30 complainants (Moneycontrol). Say whose number it is. ₹100 crore is a preliminary estimate.
The Zhibao 60% fall is to 23 Oct; don't imply it's today's price. No advice on which app to use or whether to hold US stocks.
Bets: B1 (stake: 'your US shares'), B3 (app vs broker blame is the forwardable line), B4 (split screen: the sell list against '3 lakh shares, Zhibao').

stories.title: Samvat 2082: the worst Diwali-to-Diwali year in 15 years, then the best pre-Diwali week in decades; the Sensex's loss halved from -11.9% to about -6%
stories.label: RISING
stories.window: To Sun 8 Nov (Muhurat trading, when Samvat 2082 ends). Post Fri or Sat.
happening: Samvat 2082 opened with the Sensex at 84,484.67 and the Nifty at 25,901.20. By Fri 30 Oct they were at 74,459.53 and 23,053.10, about -11.9% and -11%: set to be the worst Samvat in 15 years (ET Now, 2 Nov; Business Standard, 5 Nov).

Then six straight up days: the Sensex closed Thu 5 Nov at 79,310.01, +6,063.98 points (8.27%) in six sessions (Business Today; Times of India). Against the Samvat's opening level that's now about -6.1% on the Sensex and about -5.3% on the Nifty (our calculation from those closes).

Business Standard's headline this morning: 'Sensex up 6,064 pts in six days; eyes strongest pre-Diwali rally in 35 yrs' (6 Nov; page not opened, paywalled). The Core: 'Nifty posts best weekly performance in 5 years as FIIs step up buying' (6 Nov).
Last Diwali, analysts suggested the Nifty could reach 30,000 and the Sensex 95,000 by this Diwali (Analytics Insight, Oct 2025, context).
curiosity_gaps: A year that was heading for the worst Diwali-to-Diwali result in 15 years got half its loss back in one week. Anyone who sold in October sold at the bottom of the year.
Last Diwali's forecast was Nifty 30,000. The Nifty is at about 24,500, and the brokers have new Diwali picks out again.
